DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //wwn.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 122 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 MS. MARY JEMENY V. YULO Secretary to the Sanggunian City of Imus Province of Cavite Dear Ms. Yulo: This has reference to your letter dated 07 September 2021 seeking legal opinion from this Department regarding the proper determination of the quorum for the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Imus. Per your representation, the City of Imus is a component city with twelve (12) elected sangguniang panlungsod members and two ex-officio members of the sanggunian (the Liga ng mga Barangay President and the SK president). You also represented that the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Imus adopted an Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) through Resolution No. 04-2019-01 dated July 8, 2019 which provides for the quorum, viz: "Section 16. Quorum. A quorum shall be 50% plus 1 of all the members of the Sanggunian Panlungsod or nine (9) members and shall be determined on the basis of physical presence." According to you, there is a need to clarify from this Department whether the quorum for the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Imus is eight (8) or nine (9) in order that the sanggunian may amend its IRP. Hence, the instant request for clarification. At the outset, please be informed that the issue at hand has long been settled by the Department. It is imperative that we discuss, for purposes of clarity, the terms "quorum", "majority" "simple majority" and "qualified majority" Quorum A quorum is defined by Section 53 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 , as referring to the presence of the maioritv of all members of the sangqunian who have been duly elected and qualified. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In determining a quorum in the sanggunian, a majority of all members of the sanggunian who have been elected shall constitute a quorum. Along this line, it bears to emphasize that per Section 457 (a) of the LGC, the Sanggunian Panlungsod is a composite body where the Vice-Mayor as Presiding Officer is a composite member thereof. As a composite member in the sanggunian panlungsod, he/she is therefore included in the determination of a quorum.l Let it be noted that the Presiding Officer should be counted for purposes Of ascertaining the existence of a quorum, but not in the determination of the required number of votes necessary to uphold a matter before the sanggunian.2 Majority "Majority" has been defined by the Supreme Court in the case of Santiago V. Guingona, et al.3 as that which is qreater than half of the membership of the body or that number which is 50% + 1 of the entire membership. Simple Majority Simple majority is that which is the maiority of the members present, there being a quorum.4 Generally, ordinary measures require for its enactment only the approval of a simple majority of the sanggunian members present, there being a quorum.. These pertain to the normal transactions of the sanggunian which are approved by the sanggunian through a vote of simple majority of those present.5 For the sanggunian to officially transact business, there should be a quorum. Qualified Majority On the other hand, there are certain measures where the Local Government Code requires for its approval the vote of majority of all the members who were duly elected qualified. This is what we call approval by the majority of all the members of the sanggunian duly elected and qualified regardless of whether all of them were present or not in a particular session, there being a quorum.6 It is one wherein the total membership of the sanggunian is considered in determining a majority. However, in determining the number which constitutes as the majority vote, the Vice- Mayor is excluded. The Vice-Mayor's right to vote is merely contingent and arises 1 DILG Opinion No. 13 S. 2010, 09 February 2010 2 Javier V. cadao, G.R. No. 185369, 3 August 2016 3 G.R. only when there is a tie to break.7 As the presiding officer, the vice-mayor can vote only to break a tie. In effect, the presiding officer votes when it matters the most, that is, to break a deadlock in the votes. Clearly, the vice-mayor, as presiding officer, is a "member" of the Sangguniang Panlungsod considering that he is mandated under Section 49 of RA 7160 to vote to break a tie. To construe otherwise would create an anomalous and absurd situation where the presiding officer who votes to break a tie duririg a Sanggunian session is not considered a "member" of the Sanggunian.8 In the case of Imus, Cavite, it was represented that the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Imus, Cavite consists of twelve elected SP Members and two ex-officio members of the Sanggunian. Applying the above principle, the vice-mayor of Imus, as the presiding officer, should be counted for purposes of ascertaining the existence of a quorum. Since there are 14 members and one presiding officer in the Sanggunian, the quorum should be computed in this manner: 15/2 = 7.5 (7.5 is the 50%) 7.5 + 1 = 8.5 or can be reduced to 8 It was shown above that 8 is more than half (i.e. 7.5). Hence, the total number required to constitute a quorum is only 8 and not 7.5 nor 9.9 In view of the foregoing, the total number required to constitute a quorum for the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Imus is only 8. The Sanggunian Panlungsod should amend its IRP and change the quorum from 9 to 8 members. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, ATTY. RITY OF THE SECRETARY: VIC R R.
